study_material.title: Profit, Loss and Discounts - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Every transaction question runs on three anchors: Cost Price (CP), Selling Price (SP) and Marked Price (MP). Profit and loss are always reckoned on CP; discount is always reckoned on MP. Keep those two bases straight and the whole chapter becomes multiplication by factors.
learning_objectives: Compute profit%, loss% and discount% with the correct bases
Chain markup and discount factors multiplicatively
Relate CP-of-m = SP-of-n statements to profit percentage

concepts.heading: 1. The Three Prices
concepts.body: CP = price the article is bought for; MP (list price) = price marked; SP = price actually sold at. Profit = SP - CP (if positive), Loss = CP - SP (if positive). Profit% = Profit/CP x 100 and Discount% = Discount/MP x 100. Note the different bases - this is the most tested trap.

concepts.heading: 2. Factor Arithmetic
concepts.body: A gain of g% means SP = CP x (1 + g/100); a discount of d% means SP = MP x (1 - d/100). Chains multiply: mark up 40% then discount 15% and 10% gives overall factor 1.40 x 0.85 x 0.90. Whether the net is profit or loss just depends on whether the product exceeds 1.

concepts.heading: 3. Equal Selling Prices Trap
concepts.body: If two articles sell at the same SP, one at x% profit and the other at x% loss, the trader ALWAYS loses overall, with net loss% = x^2/100. For x = 10, loss = 1%.

concepts.heading: 4. False Weights
concepts.body: A dealer selling at cost price but using a weight of w grams instead of 1000 grams gains (1000 - w)/w x 100 percent. Example: 900 g weight gives 100/900 = 11.11% profit.

concepts.heading: 5. CP of m = SP of n
concepts.body: If the cost price of m articles equals the selling price of n articles (m > n), profit% = (m - n)/n x 100. If m < n it is a loss. Example: CP of 12 = SP of 10 gives profit of 2/10 = 20%.

formulas: CP of m = SP of n: profit% = (m-n)/n x 100
shortcut_methods: Work with multiplying factors (1.2, 0.85) instead of percentages
Successive discounts a% and b% = a + b - ab/100 overall
To find MP: MP = SP / (1 - d/100); to find CP: CP = SP / (1 + g/100)
common_mistakes: Calculating profit% on SP instead of CP
Calculating discount% on CP instead of MP
Adding successive discounts instead of combining them multiplicatively
Assuming equal profit/loss percentages at equal SP cancel out - they never do
study_material.summary: Convert every percentage into a factor, multiply the chain from CP to SP, and remember: profit sits on CP, discount sits on MP.
quick_revision_notes: Profit on CP, discount on MP
Equal SP with +x% and -x% = x^2/100 loss
SP of n = CP of m: profit = (m-n)/n x 100

solved_examples.question: An article bought for Rs. 500 is sold for Rs. 600. Find the profit percent.
A trader sells an item for Rs. 480 at a loss of 20%. Find the cost price.
A shopkeeper marks goods 25% above cost and allows a 10% discount. Find his profit percent.
solved_examples.shortcut: 25 - 10 - 250/100 = 12.5 using a + b + ab/100 with signs.

solved_examples.question: A dealer sells goods at cost price but uses a 900 g weight for 1 kg. Find his gain percent.
solved_examples.step_by_step: He charges for 1000 g but delivers 900 g. Gain% = 100/900 x 100 = 11.11%.

solved_examples.question: Two articles are each sold at Rs. 990 - one at 10% profit, the other at 10% loss. Find the overall result.
solved_examples.step_by_step: CPs are 900 and 1100, total 2000. Total SP = 1980. Loss = 20 on 2000 = 1%.
